PullRequest.Title: Fixes #347106: keep Cmd/Ctrl+B, Cmd/Ctrl+O, Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+E and Ctrl+Shift+G in the chat window that has focus
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #347106

In a chat window of the Agents window, Cmd/Ctrl+B toggled the main window's side bar, and Cmd/Ctrl+O (**New Session in Folder...**) showed its folder pick in the chat window but started the new session in the main window. With a new session (an unsent composer) active in a chat window, Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+E (**Files**) and Ctrl+Shift+G (**Changes**) opened the Files or Changes view in the main window's auxiliary bar instead of a tab in the chat window.

## Reproduction

Agents window with a sent chat moved into a chat window (**Open in New Window**), with the chat window focused.

**Before**:
- Cmd+B hid the main window's side bar.
- Cmd+O showed the pick in the chat window, and picking a folder switched the main window's composer to that folder; the chat window was unchanged.

**After**:
- Cmd+B does nothing in a chat window, which has no side bar of its own; the main window's side bar keeps its state. Cmd+B in the main window still toggles its side bar.
- Cmd+O opens the new session in the chat window, as a tab of its active chat, aimed at the picked folder, as Cmd+N opens one there. The main window's composer is untouched. Cmd+O in the main window is unchanged.

## Root cause

- **Cmd/Ctrl+B**: this is an incomplete fix of c4e701c52876 (#346039). That change gave the Agents window's **Toggle Side Bar** a `LayoutModeContext.negate()` precondition so that its key would not apply in chat windows. VS Code's own **Toggle Primary Side Bar Visibility** (`workbench.action.toggleSidebarVisibility`) is also loaded in the Agents window, through the editor and part contributions, and binds the same key with no precondition. With the Agents rule out of the way, it took the key and toggled the main layout. The test of that change checked the command id, not how the key resolves.
- **Cmd/Ctrl+O**: long-standing. The command always called `ISessionsService.openNewSession`, which targets the main window. #346678 made Cmd+N start a new session in the chat window it runs in, but not this command.

## Fix

- `workbench.action.toggleSidebarVisibility` no longer applies in a window with layout modes (`LayoutModeContext.negate()`, as the Agents window's toggle and the terminal's Move to Panel do). In VS Code, where `LayoutModeContext` is unset, nothing changes.
- **New Session in Folder...** resolves the chat window it runs in (`resolveChatWindow`, as Cmd+N does) and opens the new session there through `IChatWindowService.openNewChat`, with a new, provider-neutral `folder` option (`{ uri, providerId? }`). Elsewhere it does what it did.
- The Agents chat window provider opens a new composer aimed at that folder:
  - It always opens a new composer, whose draft goes through the composer's own creation path, including its workspace trust prompt. It never re-aims an existing composer.
  - When the active chat is a composer whose closing loses nothing (no input, no request under way, checked again once the new composer shows), the new one replaces it. A composer with input, or with a request under way, is kept, and the new one opens as a tab beside it.
  - Plain Cmd/Ctrl+N is unchanged: it reveals an unsent composer.
  - A composer opened from a composer joins the custom group of the sessions list that this composer's sessions join.
  - When the picked folder came with the provider that resolved it before (a recent folder), the composer starts with that provider's first session type for the folder, so that this provider creates its draft, as a new session in a folder of a provider starts in the main window.
  - When that provider cannot serve the folder at that moment, the composer behaves as picking that folder in the composer itself does: its picked or preferred agent, with that provider as the fallback, and its agent picker shows which one it uses. This differs from the main window, where `openNewSession` with a provider that is not available fails without a draft.

## Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+E and Ctrl+Shift+G with a new session in a chat window

**Before**: with an unsent composer active in a chat window, Cmd+Shift+E opened the Files view in the main window's auxiliary bar; with a sent chat active it opened a Files tab in the chat window. Changes (Ctrl+Shift+G) behaved the same.

**Root cause**:
- In a chat window, the Agents window's Files and Changes keys apply while the chat window's session has a workspace (`SessionWithWorkspaceContext`). `setHostSessionContextKeys` took that workspace from the chat the host shows only. A composer shows no chat until its session is created, in its chat editor and in its chat window's host, so its session counted as one without a workspace, although its draft has a folder.
- Where those keys did not apply, the open commands of the Files and Changes view containers, which `ViewsService` registers with the same keys, claimed them and opened the main window's auxiliary bar. A quick chat in a chat window, sent or not, has no workspace, so its keys did the same.
- Long-standing: new sessions in chat windows come from #346678; quick chats in chat windows had the fallthrough before that.

**Fix**:
- `setHostSessionContextKeys`: the workspace is that of the chat the host shows, or that of the session while it shows no chat of it, such as a composer's draft. A chat without a workspace still counts as one. The callers that pass a session without a chat are the composer's chat editor and the chat window's host; the main window's grid and the automations dialog always pass a chat.
- `ViewsService`: the keybinding of a view container's open command no longer applies in a window with layout modes (`LayoutModeContext.negate()` added to its `when`), whose parts are not the main window's. The commands themselves, in the Command Palette or run by code, are unchanged.

**Breadth of the `ViewsService` change**: view container open commands with keybindings are Files (Cmd+Shift+E) and Changes (Ctrl+Shift+G), both Agents window only and both opening the main window's auxiliary bar, and VS Code's Explorer, Extensions and Run and Debug, which are not registered in the Agents window. Chat, Search and SCM register no view container open command; Markers, Output, Terminal and Chat bind their keys to view open commands, which are unchanged. `LayoutModeContext` is only set in chat windows, so VS Code is unchanged.

## Tests

- `src/vs/sessions/test/browser/layoutActions.test.ts`: resolves the actual Cmd/Ctrl+B key through `KeybindingResolver` over all default keybindings on macOS, Linux and Windows, in the main Agents window, in a chat window and in VS Code. Failed before the fix, with the key resolving to `workbench.action.toggleSidebarVisibility` in a chat window.
- `src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/newSessionFolderQuickPickAction.test.ts`: the command opens the picked folder's session in the chat window it runs in, and in the main window elsewhere. Failed before the fix.
- `src/vs/workbench/contrib/sessions/test/common/sessionContextKeys.test.ts`: a host showing a session with a workspace but no chat of it publishes the session's workspace; once it shows a chat without a workspace, it publishes none. Failed before the fix.
- `src/vs/workbench/services/views/test/browser/viewsService.test.ts` (new): the keybinding of a view container's open command applies in a window without layout modes and not in one with them. Failed before the fix.
- `src/vs/sessions/contrib/chatWindow/test/browser/sessionsChatWindowProvider.test.ts`: a composer aimed at the folder with its provider's session type, opened from a sent chat; a composer that loses nothing replaced; composers with input or with a request under way kept; a composer that gets input while the new one opens kept; the custom group inherited from a composer.

Validation:
- `./scripts/test.sh --run` on the five files above: 80 passing.
- `./scripts/test.sh --runGlob` over all of `vs/sessions` and the chat window, sessions, session changes, views and workbench part test folders: 10795 passing, 0 failing.
- `pnpm run typecheck-client`, `pnpm run valid-layers-check`, and eslint on the changed files: all pass.

## Live verification

A Code - OSS build of this branch, in the Agents window (`--agents`), with a chat window holding a sent chat. The automation ran with the windows in the background, so a focused chat window was simulated: CDP focus emulation on the chat window only, plus `document.hasFocus` returning true there and false in the main window. The workbench confirmed it: `IChatWindowService.activeWindow` was the chat window for every chat window step.

- Cmd+B in the chat window: the main side bar keeps its state, both hidden and shown. Before: it toggled.
- Cmd+B in the main window: toggles its side bar, as before.
- Cmd+O in the chat window with the sent chat active: a **New Session** tab opens beside it in the chat window, with its workspace picker, title bar and terminal on the picked folder. The main window's composer is unchanged. Before: the main window's composer switched to the folder.
- Cmd+O again with that untouched composer active: it is replaced by one for the next folder.
- Cmd+O with text typed in the composer: it keeps its text and folder, and a new tab opens for the picked folder.
- Cmd+O in the main window: the main window's composer moves to the picked folder; the chat window is unchanged.
- Cmd+Shift+E and Ctrl+Shift+G in the chat window with a sent chat active: a Files tab, then a Changes tab of that chat, open in the chat window.
- Cmd+Shift+E and Ctrl+Shift+G with a new session (from Cmd+N) active in the chat window: the Files tab and a Changes tab open in the chat window. The main window's auxiliary bar stays closed. Before: Cmd+Shift+E opened the Files view in the main window's auxiliary bar.
- Cmd+Shift+E and Ctrl+Shift+G in a chat window with a quick chat, sent or a new one: nothing happens; the main window's auxiliary bar stays closed.
- Cmd+Shift+E and Ctrl+Shift+G in the main window: Files and Changes open there, as before.

## Review

Reviewed by a separate reviewer on a different model across design, correctness, patterns, performance and lifecycle, security and trust, compatibility, UX, tests and hygiene. Its findings (re-aiming a mounted composer only changed its metadata; a composer with a request under way counted as unsent; the folder's provider was only a fallback; a race while the new composer opened; the custom group lost from a composer) are fixed in the later commits. The Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+E fix was reviewed by the same reviewer, including every caller of `setHostSessionContextKeys` and every view container open command with a keybinding. Final verdict: approved, with no known actionable findings.

Scenarios.Scenario: Cmd/Ctrl+O selects a recent folder while a chat window has focus and opens a new-session composer there
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Build the existing in-memory quick-pick items, await one user selection, resolve the focused chat window, synchronously derive a target, create one draft slot/composer, and await opening one editor in the existing chat window. No subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network operation was found on the newly introduced target-resolution path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open and render one chat editor/composer in the existing auxiliary window
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one editor open per accepted folder selection; no collection fan-out or aggregate concurrency
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same command instead invoked ISessionsService.openNewSession in the main window, creating/activating one main-window draft/session view.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The command awaits the editor open before completing

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected folder and the small registered-provider set. getSessionTypesForFolder scans providers synchronously once only when a providerId accompanies the recent; concrete providers perform URI/metadata checks without boundary I/O, and the Copilot provider's optional repository resolution remains lazy and bounded by a 50-entry state cache.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The command schedules one open. ChatWindowService serializes opens per chat resource; this unique composer resource creates no burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Recent workspaces are consumed from existing service state. Folder-type lookup has no separate result cache, but runs once per explicit command; provider repository metadata state is reused and bounded. There is no negative-cache retry loop on this path.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from tracing the changed command through SessionsChatWindowContent.openNewChat, ChatWindowComposers.create, getSessionTypesForFolder, and ChatWindowService._addChat.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual editor-render latency varies with machine and loaded contributions, but the diff does not multiply the work or add an expensive external boundary.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff intentionally redirects one user-triggered operation to one composer in the focused window; added provider work is bounded synchronous metadata work, and composer ownership/disposal is explicit.

Scenarios.Scenario: Cmd/Ctrl+O uses Browse in either the main Agents window or a chat window
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Await the existing OS folder picker once, then follow either the unchanged main-window open path or the new one-composer chat-window path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Show the platform folder-open dialog and return one selected URI
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One dialog invocation per Browse selection
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same Browse branch and single dialog call existed before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Folder selection must complete before a session/composer can open

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open one editor/composer in the focused chat window after selection
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One open for one selected folder
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The selected folder was passed to one main-window ISessionsService.openNewSession call.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: A single selected folder; Browse clears providerId, so the new _getFolderTarget path does not scan providers at command time.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Fully sequential: dialog, then one open. No Promise.all or per-provider external operations.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache affects the OS dialog. Composer creation allocates one fresh draft slot by design; no repeated miss behavior was found.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the complete action branch and target construction.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: OS dialog latency is environment-dependent but unchanged by this PR.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression. The only filesystem/OS boundary is pre-existing and remains one call; changed post-selection work is bounded to one editor.

Scenarios.Scenario: Opening a picked folder from a pristine, edited, or sending chat-window composer
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Create and show one new composer first; if the prior composer was pristine both before and after the open, close its editor and dispose its draft slot. Edited or sending composers remain open.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open one new editor and, for a still-pristine predecessor, close one old editor
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one open and one close per command
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: A folder command did not target the chat window, so no chat-window composer replacement occurred.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both operations are awaited; closing occurs only after the new editor successfully shows

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Constant cardinality independent of session history, tab count, or input size. The old and new composers overlap only for the duration of one editor open.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One sequential editor open followed by at most one close; no unbounded concurrent composer construction or cleanup.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Each composer owns one draft slot. Closing disposes the composer, removes it from the live map, and disposes/discards its slot; failed opens clean the pending composer in finally.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the explicit pending-composer finally cleanup, editor-owned composer disposal, and post-open pristine check.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Editor-open duration is variable, but overlap is bounded to one predecessor and one replacement.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable cleanup, retention, or concurrency regression. Replacement temporarily holds one extra lightweight composer to preserve data safely, then deterministically disposes it.

Scenarios.Scenario: Cmd/Ctrl+B and view-container keybindings resolve in main, chat, and normal VS Code windows
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Default keybinding resolution evaluates an added context expression/precondition and either dispatches the existing command or leaves the key unclaimed.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One constant-size context-expression evaluation per relevant keypress; view-container rules are registered once per contributed container as before.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous single-event dispatch with no queued or parallel work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache or miss path is involved.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the changed action descriptors and view action registration.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material; the changed mechanism is a constant-time predicate.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance issue. The changes suppress incorrect command dispatch and avoid, rather than add, layout/view work in chat windows.

Scenarios.Scenario: Session host context keys update while a composer has a session workspace but no shown chat
Scenarios.CriticalPath: An existing autorun now reads session.workspace when chat is absent and writes the same two context keys; when a chat exists it keeps reading chat.workspace.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One observable read and two existing context-key writes per relevant reactive update, independent of workspace file count and session history.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous reactive update in the existing autorun; no asynchronous scheduling or fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Observable dependency tracking supplies updates; no new cache, serialization, or external fetch is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from all callers and the direct observable read in setHostSessionContextKeys.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Workspace update frequency depends on provider state, but the added work per update is constant and local.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable synchronous UI or repeated-work regression; the new fallback is constant-time and does not cross an expensive boundary.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 12 changed files and all patch pages. Traced command routing, provider target resolution, composer allocation/replacement/cleanup, editor opening, context-key updates, and keybinding registration. No high-confidence actionable performance regression or qualifying regression fix was found.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
